newsitem.title: EGYPT: Housing firm still tops as Egypt shares slip.
newsitem.headline: Housing firm still tops as Egypt shares slip.

text.p: Egyptian share prices slipped slightly on Thursday in trade still dominated by Heliopolis Housing and Development, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) overall index closed 0.38 points lower at 287.76 while volume was a healthy 55.02 million pounds.
"It was a normal day today. The market is growing and volume in the fifties like today is becoming a usual thing," said Mohammed Magdi of EFG/Herms brokerage.
"Today's small drop is not that significant a change to worry about," he added.
Heliopolis was the day's most active stock, accounting for 14.92 million pounds of the day's turnover after the share jumped 15.00 pounds to end trading at 335.00.
"The demand on Heliopolis is high and the shares are not easy to find," said Magdi.
The firm announced on Monday that it had almost doubled profits in the 1995/6 financial year to 61.35 million pounds.
Brokers have said that the government -- which had offered five or more percent of the firm to strategic investors -- was selling some of its majority stake through the bourse.
Helwan Cement was the second most active stock but it fell 1.45 pounds to 61.30 after shares worth more than 8.16 million pounds exchanged hands.

The popular milling sector saw small price changes in both directions. Central and Western Flour Mills closed 0.99 pounds lower at 85 but East Delta Flour Mills rose 1.35 pounds to close at 54.35 while Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed 0.25 pounds higher at 69.50.
The CMA index for openly traded firms fell to 434.81 from 435.69 points on Wednesday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 201.82 from 202.01 points.
